passages.text: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The Spirit led Jesus.
The Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness.
The devil tempted Jesus in the wilderness.
passages.original: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου

passages.text: After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The Holy Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness.
Jesus fasted for forty days.
Jesus fasted for forty nights.
After this, Jesus became hungry.
passages.original: καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ τεσσεράκοντα νύκτας ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν

passages.text: The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”
passages.sermon:
The tempter came to Jesus.
The tempter spoke to Jesus.
The tempter said, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
The tempter challenged Jesus to prove His identity as the Son of God.
The tempter told Jesus to command the stones to turn into bread.
passages.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται

passages.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus answered the tempter.
Jesus said, “It is written.”
Man does not live on bread alone.
Man lives on every word that comes from the mouth of God.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Γέγραπται Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος Ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος Θεοῦ

passages.text: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.
passages.sermon:
The devil is God's enemy.
The devil took Jesus.
Jesus is the Son of God.
The devil brought Jesus to the holy city.
The holy city is Jerusalem.
The devil set Jesus on the highest point of the temple.
The highest point is called the pinnacle of the temple.
passages.original: Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ

passages.text: “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down. For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’”
passages.sermon:
The devil spoke to Jesus.
The devil said, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down."
The devil referred to what is written in Scripture.
He said, "God will command His angels about you."
He said, "The angels will lift you up in their hands."
He said, "You will not strike your foot against a stone."
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μή‿ ποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου

passages.text: Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the devil.\r\nJesus said, “It is written again.”\r\nJesus said, “Do not test the Lord your God.”
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πάλιν γέγραπται Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου

passages.text: Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
passages.sermon:
The devil took Jesus again.
The devil led Jesus to a very high mountain.
The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world.
The devil showed Jesus the glory of these kingdoms.
passages.original: Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν

passages.text: “All this I will give You,” he said, “if You will fall down and worship me.”
passages.sermon:
The devil spoke to Jesus.
The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
The devil said, “I will give You all these things.”
The devil said, “You must fall down and worship me.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι

passages.text: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus declared. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Satan.
Jesus said, “Go away, Satan.”
Jesus said, “It is written.”
Jesus said, “Worship the Lord your God.”
Jesus said, “Serve only Him.”
passages.original: Τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὕπαγε Σατανᾶ γέγραπται γάρ Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις

passages.text: Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The devil tempted Jesus.
Jesus refused the devil.
The devil left Jesus.
Angels came to Jesus.
The angels served Jesus.
passages.original: Τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ

passages.text: When Jesus heard that John had been imprisoned, He withdrew to Galilee.
passages.sermon: Jesus heard that John was put in prison.\r\nJesus then left the place where He was.\r\nJesus went to Galilee.
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάννης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν

passages.text: Leaving Nazareth, He went and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali, to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles— the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus left Nazareth.
He went to live in Capernaum.
Capernaum is by the sea.
Capernaum is in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Jesus did this to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah said.
Isaiah spoke these words:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali,
The Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan,
Galilee of the Gentiles.
The people living in darkness have seen a great light.
A light has dawned on those living in the land of the shadow of death.”
passages.original: καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλίμ ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλίμ ὁδὸν θαλάσσης πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
John the Baptist had been imprisoned.
After this, Jesus began to preach.
Jesus said, “Repent.”
He said, “The kingdom of heaven is near.”
passages.original: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς κηρύσσειν καὶ λέγειν Μετανοεῖτε ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee.
He saw two brothers.
One brother was Simon, who was also called Peter.
The other brother was Andrew.
Simon and Andrew were casting a net into the sea.
They were fishermen.
passages.original: Περιπατῶν δὲ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν δύο ἀδελφούς Σίμωνα τὸν λεγόμενον Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ βάλλοντας ἀμφίβληστρον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς

passages.text: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the two brothers.\r\nHe said, “Come, follow Me.”\r\nHe promised, “I will make you fishers of men.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew were fishermen.
Jesus called them to follow Him.
Immediately, they left their nets.
They followed Jesus.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them, and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked further from where He was.
He saw two other brothers.
Their names were James and John.
James was the son of Zebedee.
John was James’s brother.
James and John were in a boat.
Their father Zebedee was with them.
They were mending their nets.
Jesus called James and John.
James and John immediately left the boat.
They left their father Zebedee.
They followed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ προβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄλλους δύο ἀδελφούς Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ Ζεβεδαίου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὸ πλοῖον καὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled through all of Galilee.
He taught in their synagogues.
He preached the good news about the kingdom.
He healed every disease among the people.
He healed every sickness among the people.
passages.original: Καὶ περιῆγεν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν ἐν τῷ λαῷ

passages.text: News about Him spread all over Syria, and people brought to Him all who were ill with various diseases, those suffering acute pain, the demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed—and He healed them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus became known throughout all Syria.
People heard about Him everywhere in that region.
People brought to Jesus everyone who was sick.
Some people had many different diseases.
Some people suffered great pain.
Some people were possessed by demons.
Some people had seizures.
Some people could not walk.
Jesus healed all of them.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν Συρίαν καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις καὶ βασάνοις συνεχομένους καὶ δαιμονιζομένους καὶ σεληνιαζομένους καὶ παραλυτικούς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς

passages.text: The large crowds that followed Him came from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled through Galilee.
He taught in the synagogues.
He preached the good news of the kingdom.
He healed every disease and sickness among the people.
Many people heard about Jesus.
Large crowds followed Jesus.
These crowds came from Galilee.
Some came from the Decapolis.
Some came from Jerusalem.
Some came from Judea.
Others came from beyond the Jordan.
passages.original: Καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Δεκαπόλεως καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου
